title: Notice pleading and its development
summary: Notice pleading emphasizes giving the opposing party an intelligible account of the claim and its grounds without requiring the technical formulas of older pleading systems. The assigned cases trace its development and later qualifications.
notes: Conley’s no-set-of-facts formulation was expressly retired in Twombly. A historical statement should remain visible as history, rather than be placed beside the later standard as if both formulations were interchangeable.

sections.How to work through the question: Use Dioguardi and Conley to understand the notice function, Swierkiewicz to separate evidence frameworks from pleading, and Twombly and Iqbal to identify the later plausibility requirement.
